nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer sun powers the open, treeless grassland and the shallow wetlands that make up the puszta.

nodes.name: Alkaline soils
nodes.desc: Salty, alkaline soils on the Great Plain keep much of the puszta treeless and favour salt-tolerant grasses and herbs.

nodes.name: Tisza River floods
nodes.desc: The Tisza shaped this plain; its changing course is thought to have started the alkalinisation of the soils about 10,000 years ago.

nodes.name: Marshes and fishponds
nodes.desc: Marshes and artificial fishponds, first dug in 1914-1918 and again in the 1950s, add reed beds and open water to the grassland.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and soil invertebrates break down dung, dead grass and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Puszta grasses
nodes.desc: Short, hardy grasses and herbs of the alkaline pastures; they feed the grazers and are kept short by them.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Reed beds line the marshes and fishponds, giving food and cover to geese, herons and harriers.

nodes.name: Hoary cress
nodes.desc: A crucifer of open ground and field edges; crucifers are among the plants great bustards eat.

nodes.name: Hungarian Grey cattle
nodes.desc: A hardy landrace long herded on the puszta by mounted csikos. Grazing keeps the pasture open and short.

nodes.name: Przewalski's horse
nodes.desc: A small herd of about 25 of these wild horses lives in the park, grazing the steppe much as wild horses did in the Ice Age.

nodes.name: European ground squirrel
nodes.desc: A burrowing grazer that needs short turf, which grazing maintains. It eats plants, seeds and insects and is a main prey of saker falcons.

nodes.name: European hamster
nodes.desc: A burrowing rodent of grassland and fields that eats seeds and plants and is taken by foxes and many raptors.

nodes.name: Meadow brown
nodes.desc: A common grassland butterfly whose caterpillars eat grasses; adults and larvae feed birds and frogs.

nodes.name: Greylag goose
nodes.desc: A large grazing goose of wetland and meadows that eats reed shoots and grasses.

nodes.name: Common crane
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats mostly plant matter, waste grain, insects, frogs and small rodents. Big numbers pass through Hungary on migration.

nodes.name: Great bustard
nodes.desc: Hungary's national bird eats green plants, seeds and insects. Foxes and crows are serious predators of its eggs and chicks.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: A large water frog of ponds and canals that eats insects and other small animals and is food for herons, snakes and eagles.

nodes.name: Grass snake
nodes.desc: A semi-aquatic snake that hunts frogs and other amphibians around ponds and wet meadows.

nodes.name: Grey heron
nodes.desc: A wading bird that spears frogs, snakes and small mammals at the edges of fishponds and in wet grassland.

nodes.name: Western marsh harrier
nodes.desc: A raptor of reed beds that hunts frogs, snakes and small mammals over wetlands and nearby fields.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: A generalist that takes rodents, ground squirrels, birds and their eggs, frogs and carrion.

nodes.name: Saker falcon
nodes.desc: A falcon of open steppe whose main prey in Europe is ground squirrels and pigeons; it often nests in old stick nests in trees.

nodes.name: White-tailed eagle
nodes.desc: A huge eagle around the fishponds and marshes that takes waterbirds, mammals and amphibians and also eats carrion.
